| [LIT-505](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-505.md) v2 | Biological structure and function emerge from scaling unsupervised learning to 250 million protein sequences | Rives et al. (2021), PNAS 118(15) — the protein language model the biological-sequence line runs from. A transformer trained by masked-token prediction on 250 million protein sequences, with no structural or functional labels, produces representations in which secondary structure, tertiary contacts and remote homology are linearly recoverable. Held here as the ancestor of [LIT-506](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-506.md), which reimplements the recipe for RNA and copies its downstream head. | Active |
| [LIT-506](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-506.md) v2 | Interpretable RNA Foundation Model from Unannotated Data for Highly Accurate RNA Structure and Function Predictions | Chen et al. (2022), [ARXIV-2204.00300](https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.00300) — a 12-layer BERT encoder trained by masked-token prediction on **23.7 million** unannotated ncRNA sequences from RNAcentral, then used as a frozen feature extractor for secondary structure, 3D contact, protein-RNA binding and UTR regulation. Beats twelve secondary-structure methods (F1 **0.941** on ArchiveII600, **0.704** on bpRNA TS0). Read as [NOTE-252](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-252.md), which records that the paper's one clean input-swap control moves `R²` by **0.002** on the generalization set. | Active |
| [LIT-583](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-583.md) | Highly accurate protein structure prediction with AlphaFold | Jumper et al. (Nature 2021), DOI 10.1038/s41586-021-03819-2. AlphaFold 2 predicts protein structure from sequence and a multiple sequence alignment. At CASP14 its median backbone error was 0.96 Å r.m.s.d.95, against 2.8 Å for the next best method. Its per-residue confidence, pLDDT, tracks true accuracy (r = 0.76 over 10,795 chains). Self-distillation on its own confident predictions for 350,000 unlabeled sequences improves it. Accuracy falls sharply when the alignment has fewer than about 30 sequences. | Active |
| [LIT-584](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-584.md) | Accurate structure prediction of biomolecular interactions with AlphaFold 3 | Abramson et al. (Nature 2024), DOI 10.1038/s41586-024-07487-w. AlphaFold 3 predicts complexes of proteins, nucleic acids, ligands, ions and modified residues. A pairformer with lighter MSA processing replaces the Evoformer, and a diffusion module over raw atom coordinates replaces the structure module, with no built-in rotational equivariance. It beats Vina on PoseBusters without the pocket information Vina gets (P = 2.27×10⁻¹³). The generative head hallucinates structure in disordered regions, which cross-distillation from AlphaFold-Multimer reduces. Chirality is violated in 4.4% of PoseBusters predictions even after ranking penalties. | Active |
| [LIT-679](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-679.md) | Dynamic Chunking for End-to-End Hierarchical Sequence Modeling | Hwang, Wang and Gu (2025; ICLR 2026), [ARXIV-2507.07955](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.07955). H-Net is a byte-level hierarchical model that learns where to cut chunks. Compared with a GPT-2 BPE Transformer at **matched bytes per batch and FLOPs per byte**, a chain of baselines separates each ingredient. **One stage of learned chunking only ties BPE and whitespace chunking** (0.728 against 0.730 against 0.726 bits/byte at XL). The gain is the **second stage** (0.715, +2.7 downstream average). The largest gains are on Chinese. It is limited to 1.3B-equivalent FLOPs and trains about 2× slower in wall-clock. | Active |
| [LIT-702](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-702.md) | Simple and Effective Masked Diffusion Language Models | Sahoo et al. (2024), [ARXIV-2406.07524](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.07524). MDLM: the masked-diffusion training objective reduces to a weighted average of BERT-style masked-LM losses, a continuous-time ELBO whose value is invariant to the noise schedule. It is the strongest discrete diffusion language model at its scale — beating SEDD at matched tokens — and still trails a retrained autoregressive baseline in-domain (LM1B 27.04 vs 22.32; OWT 23.21 vs 17.54), which the authors state as the limitation. | Active |
| [LIT-754](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-754.md) | Efficient AlphaFold2 Training using Parallel Evoformer and Branch Parallelism | Wang et al. (2022), [ARXIV-2211.00235](https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.00235). Move the Evoformer's outer product mean to the end of the block, so the MSA and pair stacks no longer depend on each other within a block; this matches the original block's accuracy and speed. Then put the two stacks on two GPUs. On a batch of one protein per device, where data parallelism cannot scale further, this cuts end-to-end AlphaFold2 training from 5.8 to 4.2 days on UniFold and from 6.7 to 4.9 days on HelixFold, using twice the GPUs. | Active |
| [LIT-808](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-808.md) | Open Graph Benchmark: Datasets for Machine Learning on Graphs | Hu, Fey, Zitnik, Dong, Ren, Liu, Catasta, Leskovec (NeurIPS 2020), [ARXIV-2005.00687](https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.00687). Fifteen node, link and graph datasets, from 4k to 111M nodes, each with an application-driven split (time, species, scaffold, protein target, project) and a fixed evaluator. On every dataset where the authors also ran a random split of the same proportions, the same model scores higher on it: 88.2 against 78.5% on ogbn-products, 82.7 against 77.1 ROC-AUC on ogbg-molhiv, 92.9 against 70.4% on ogbg-ppa. | Active |
| [LIT-825](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-825.md) | SchNet: A continuous-filter convolutional neural network for modeling quantum interactions | Schütt et al. (NeurIPS 2017), [ARXIV-1706.08566](https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.08566). Message passing over atoms whose filters are generated by a network from interatomic distances, so the energy is rotation-invariant and smooth, and forces taken as its negative gradient are energy-conserving. QM9 U0 MAE 0.31 kcal/mol at 110k training molecules. On MD17 with 1,000 configurations, training on energies and forces cuts force MAE 17–46× against energies alone (benzene 14.12 → 0.31 kcal/mol/Å), and beats energy-only training on 50,000 on forces. The kernel baseline GDML still has the lower force error on 6 of 8 molecules. | Active |
| [LIT-829](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-829.md) | Neural Message Passing for Quantum Chemistry | Gilmer, Schoenholz, Riley, Vinyals, Dahl (ICML 2017), [ARXIV-1704.01212](https://arxiv.org/abs/1704.01212). Message Passing Neural Networks name the common form of eight earlier graph models: T rounds of messages summed over neighbors, a node update, and a permutation-invariant readout. An MPNN with edge-network messages, set2set readout and explicit hydrogens reaches chemical accuracy on 11 of 13 QM9 targets, with an average error ratio of 0.68 against 1.35 for the best hand-engineered baseline. That is one random split, with no repeated runs. | Active |
| [LIT-843](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-843.md) | Do Transformers Really Perform Bad for Graph Representation? | Ying, Cai, Luo, Zheng, Ke, He, Shen, Liu (NeurIPS 2021), [ARXIV-2106.05234](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.05234). A standard Transformer over all nodes, given node degree as an input embedding and a learned attention bias per shortest-path distance and per edge feature along the path. On PCQM4M-LSC it reaches validation MAE 0.1234 against GIN-VN's 0.1395, an 11.5% relative cut, with 7× the parameters; an ensemble won the OGB-LSC graph track. In a shorter ablation run the encodings take MAE from 0.2276 to 0.1304. At a matched 500k budget on ZINC it reaches MAE 0.122. | Active |
